# Base rates: five-year revenue growth

How fast do companies actually grow revenue over five years? 26,399 company-periods from SEC XBRL annual revenue, calendar 2009–2025, grouped by revenue at the start (`data/base_rates/revenue/`). Use it as the prior before any company-specific story: a forecast above the 90th percentile needs evidence that this company is one of the few.

| Starting revenue | Periods | 10th | 25th | Median | 75th | 90th | 95th | Shrank | Grew >10%/yr | Grew >20%/yr |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| $50M–$325M | 7,193 | -11.4% | +0.1% | +8.0% | +19.1% | +32.6% | +43.5% | 25% | 45% | 24% |
| $325M–$700M | 3,999 | -6.5% | -0.3% | +6.4% | +13.4% | +22.5% | +29.5% | 26% | 36% | 13% |
| $700M–$1.5B | 4,341 | -5.9% | +0.5% | +5.7% | +11.7% | +19.9% | +27.2% | 23% | 31% | 10% |
| $1.5B–$3B | 3,583 | -5.9% | +0.1% | +4.9% | +9.8% | +16.3% | +21.6% | 24% | 24% | 6% |
| $3B–$6B | 2,758 | -5.8% | +0.1% | +4.8% | +9.2% | +14.9% | +21.1% | 25% | 22% | 6% |
| $6B–$12B | 2,033 | -5.9% | -0.2% | +4.0% | +8.6% | +14.4% | +19.9% | 26% | 19% | 5% |
| $12B–$25B | 1,299 | -6.1% | -1.3% | +2.8% | +6.9% | +11.5% | +15.4% | 32% | 13% | 2% |
| $25B–$50B | 612 | -5.9% | -1.5% | +3.1% | +6.8% | +10.8% | +15.2% | 30% | 12% | 2% |
| Over $50B | 581 | -6.4% | -0.4% | +3.9% | +8.3% | +11.7% | +14.8% | 27% | 17% | 2% |

Caveats: SEC `frames` values are the latest filed, so these are restated figures (fine for a distribution, wrong for a backtest). Only companies that filed in both years count, so failures and acquisitions drop out and the distribution is biased upward. Starting revenue is nominal. The XBRL era starts in 2009.

## Coverage against the base rates

Each latest call's scenario revenue CAGR, placed in the distribution for its starting revenue (TTM revenue as filed on the call date). Percentile = share of history at or below the forecast.

Across 55 calls, the median base case sits at the 71th percentile; 27 of 55 base cases are above the 75th percentile and 18 of 55 bull cases are above the 90th.
